Subject: Pipeline stage primer + quick seller quiz & account handoff

Team —

Quick heads-up: Finance approved a concise tweak to our stage definitions (Commit / Best Case / Pipeline) to reduce ambiguity for mid‑quarter closes. The change is deliberately small but important for consistent forecast signals:

- Commit: buyer has legally reviewed SOW/PO and legal/finance approval is not blocking close within the quarter.
- Best Case: strong verbal + exec alignment, contract is in final review but still needs formal sign (no legal/finance blockers expected).
- Pipeline: active opportunity but missing either exec alignment or contract progress to be considered in Best Case.

Why this matters: the updated rules remove the "verbal-only" edge case that has been inflating Best Case across a few accounts. We ran a 30‑opportunity backfill and saw a 7% reduction in Best Case leakage into Commit.

What I need from sellers by EOD Friday (June 9):
1) Review opportunities you own in HubSpot for PioneerHealth and mark any that need status changes. Link below.
2) Complete the 6-question seller quiz (should take ~3 mins) to confirm you understand the new boundary between Commit and Best Case.
3) If you want a short calibration slot, reply with 30-min windows you have on Thursday/Friday; Marissa will run side-by-side reviews.

Attachments: stage-definitions-onepager.pdf (one-pager), seller-quiz.pdf (6 Qs).
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-stage-defs | HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/RDW-4721

Thanks — I’ll run a readout with Finance next week if any broader gaps show up.

—Olga

Good question — thanks for flagging. Short rule:

- If legal has only "acknowledged receipt" and is actively negotiating redlines that could change contract economics or timing, keep as Best Case.
- If legal confirms redlines are purely administrative (formatting, non‑substantive language) AND procurement has signaled no blocking items, move to Commit.

Concrete example: PioneerHealth deal RDW-4721 — exec sponsor has signed off, procurement queued legal review for standard NDA addendum. If legal flags no pricing or SLA changes and procurement confirms timing, RDW-4721 can be Commit; if legal lists change requests that will require another exec touchpoint, keep Best Case.

I’ll add this Q/A to the one‑pager before the readout.

—Olga
